hyps.why: With a very small learning rate the 243-epoch run is under-trained, so a larger step helps (runs 61, 65, 69).
Raising an already large learning rate causes unstable training and accuracy drops (run 64).
Reducing an excessive learning rate restores stable training (runs 74, 78).
Lowering an already small learning rate leaves the model more under-trained (runs 71, 75).
Strong L2 penalty already underfits, and more regularization hurts further (runs 3, 10).
Relaxing an overly strong L2 penalty frees the model to fit (run 20).
Large batches give few updates in 243 epochs, so smaller batches add more updates (runs 39, 40).
Even larger batches further reduce the number of optimizer steps (runs 25, 29).
Wider networks learn faster per step, which helps most when the learning rate is small and training is slow (run 89).
Very narrow networks are capacity-limited, so adding width helps (run 89).
